First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}+\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, in the last step, we simplified the right-hand side using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta (\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta })=1.
$$
